When looking at a set of numbers, extreme values can skew the average. A box plot uses the middle half of the data to draw a box, marked by the first and third quartiles.

The distance between these two quartiles is called the interquartile range, or IQR for short.

Look at the box plot in to see how fences mark the limits of expected values.

```

We find the IQR by subtracting the first quartile from the third quartile. Multiplying this range by 1.5 gives us a boundary distance.

Adding this scaled distance to the third quartile creates an upper fence, while subtracting it from the first quartile creates a lower fence. Any data point that lies beyond these fences is flagged as an outlier.
